correctness.rationale: The repaired statement holds for d≥2. Minimality is an open condition in the complex Stiefel space of stacked Kraus operators; the free U(r) gauge subtracts r² from 2rd²−d². Independently, the rank-r PSD Choi stratum has analytic Schur-complement charts, and congruence by (I+tH/2)⊗I gives any desired derivative H of the output partial trace at the trace-preserving level. Thus evaluation is analytic on the stated manifold. Each probe contributes at most d²−1 data dimensions; invariance of domain forbids an injection when the manifold dimension exceeds that of the data, including 11>9 for three qubit probes even against same-rank competitors. The listed states span the Hermitian inputs and hence determine the complex-linear map. On each connected component the highest nonzero exterior power of the differential gives the open dense maximal-rank locus; the zero-rank case is constant locally. The constant-rank theorem gives the stated smooth fibers of dimension ≥2 there. The repaired argument is analytic rather than empirical, and the sole d=1 channel needs zero probes.

value.rationale: The useful result is the sharp intermediate-rank obstruction under the same fixed experimental design for all targets: despite removing one Choi eigenvalue, universal identification still needs a full Hermitian input basis, and the failure with three inputs persists with positive-dimensional fibers on an open dense locus. This distinguishes both target-adapted smaller probe sets and isolated examples of ambiguity. Its value is this specific exact boundary, not the routine topological tools or the already known full-rank endpoint.
